mechanism_narrative: The continued rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-3w to t-0w signals a gradual return to commuting and weekday downtown footfall, which should lift retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to rise for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above +20 percent baseline while RETAIL_REC is deeply negative, discretionary trips accumulate at home; if residential stay rises further, retail visits should fall further within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 and RETAIL_REC stays below -65
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not decline below its current level within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM indicates more local out-of-home activity and errands, which should spill over into more retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improve over the next month but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines versus the prior month, the interaction claim is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls another 2 points or more from its current level, that will signal weaker access to shopping corridors and a near-term drop in retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops at least 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: A further week-on-week TRANSIT drop of 2 points or more followed by no decline in RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days rejects the signal.

mechanism_narrative: In winter conditions, park visits are a substitute for enclosed leisure trips; because PARKS are still negative and drifting lower, this substitution will keep retail-and-recreation mobility from recovering over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS begins a sustained recovery but RETAIL_REC still falls over the following month, the seasonal substitution mechanism is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: A widening gap where RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed implies persistent at-home routines and low discretionary movement, which should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 20 while TRANSIT below -65 and WORKPLACES below -54
failure_condition: If the home-vs-outside gap persists for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not decline further within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued upward slope in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rebound in RETAIL_REC indicates trips are being concentrated on necessities rather than discretionary shopping, which should leave retail-and-recreation mobility lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising for a month and RETAIL_REC rises instead of falling, the necessity-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES crosses above a less negative threshold while TRANSIT remains near its current level, return-to-office trips will not yet translate into more retail visits; only a coordinated transit rebound should raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -52 without TRANSIT rising above -66
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES improves above -52 and TRANSIT does not improve, but RETAIL_REC still rises over the next month, the claim that transit coordination is required is false.
